lawyer:
Md. Abdur Razaque Khan, Senior Advocate instructed by Zainul Abedin, Advocate-on-Record. ------ For the Petitioner. 
For the Respondents ------ None represented.
parties:
Md. Azizur Rahman. ----- Petitioner.
VS
The State and another ----- Respondents.
full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim J: This Petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated the 2nd day of June, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 737 of 2004 discharging the Rule with direction to the Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka to dispose of the case /in proceeding of G.R. Case No. 579 of 2000 arising out of Dhanmondi P.S. Case No.  56(2)2000 dated 17.02.2000 under; Section 420/468/471/109 of the Penal Code within 4(four) months from the date of receipt of the judgment. 

 2. The facts involved in the case, in short, are that the accused No. 1, Md. Rajab Ali Palowan, by opening current account No. 12897 in the complainant Bank in the I name of 'M/S. Mukta Enterprise' had been running his business. At a subsequent stage he had opened in that Bank another current account 13613 on 23.07.1997 in which the accused petition No. 2 acted as identifier. Accused petitioner No. 1 imported poultry feed from India opening the complainant Bank 20% margin letter of credit No.  UCBER B-ACU-98092 dated 16.04.1998 and letter of credit No.  UCBER B-ACU-98124 dated 17.05.1998 herein after called L/C for $ 12,2000 and $ 10,8000 (Bangladeshi TK. 5,68,215.00 and 4,86,902.00) PAD No. 135/98 and 167/98 respectively. The aforementioned imported goods reached on 23.04.1998 and 25.05.1998 respectively, the office of witness No. 6 Superintendent of Customs, Sona- Mosjid Customs Check post, police station Shibgonj, Nowabgonj. The complainant Bank on receipt of shipping documents informed the accused No. 1 by a letter dated 18.05.1998 and 11.06.1998 asking him to collect the shipping documents on payment of Banks dues against L/C by 18.06.1998 and 11.07.1998 but the  accused No. 1 by his letter dated 08.10.1998 informed the Bank that due to flood he had suffered loss in his business and as such, he will collect the shipping documents by arranging payment of the Bank dues and the accused petitioner No. 1 on 23.12.1998 verbally prayed for further time. On 09.04.1999 on payment of Tk. 10,000.00 by a letter the promised to pay the rest dues of the bank by 30.04.1999. The conduct of the accused gave raise to suspicion and as such the bank formed an enquiry committee consisted of witnesses Nos. 4, 5 and 7 of the petition of complaint to hold enquiry in to the matter as Sona Mosjid Check post. On query it revealed that the accused No. 1 collusively with the help of accused No. 3 got delivery of the imported goods from 22.04.1998 to 23.04.1998 and 16.05.1998 to 29.05.1998 without shipping documents by creation of false papers and token. The accused petitioner No. 1 having failed to repay the bank dues by 30.04.1998 and the Bank issued demand letter dated 04.05.1999 on receipt of which the accused No. 1 verbally prayed for time and by letter dated 04.07.1999 promised to pay the dues by 31.07.1999 which he ultimately did not. The accused petitioner did not pay the Bank demand money and as such, the accused petitioners occurred an offence punishable under Section 420/468/471/109 of the Penal Code. 

 4. Mr. Md. Abdur Razaque Khan, learned Counsel, appearing for the petitioner submitted that a clearing and forwarding Agent attached to Sona Masjid customs check post at the relevant period in the year 1999 for clearing of imported goods with assigned duty of payment of customs dues and there was no allegation that in clearing of goods any evasion of custom dues took place; that the allegations as made in the FIR and charge-sheet only disclose that imported goods were cleared at Sona Masjid Customs check post without taking/retiring Bank documents by the Opener and non-payment of bank dues by the accused importer and his guarantor, the co-accused of the case. The accused petitioner, a C& F Agent had nothing to do with obtaining of bank documents or payment of bank dues in the L/C opening bank at Dhaka. There was no allegation in the FIR or in the charge sheet or nay material on record that the accused petitioner used or fabricated any bank document or presented any forged bank document at Sona Masjid customs check post for clearing of imported goods from the said check post. The learned Counsel further submitted that the only allegation made out by the prosecution was non-payment of bank dues by the two co-accused, who opened the L/C but in spite of series of correspondence exchanged between the bank and the importer, made only part payment and assured of further payment but did not pay off total bank dues; that the FIR and charge sheet there was only allegation of a vague nature that the importer in collusion with the accused petitioner by fabricating papers obtained clearance of imported goods for Sona Masjid check post but in the charge sheet no alamat was shown as papers/documents or fabricated by the accused for obtaining clearance. The learned Counsel finally submitted that all SRO's and documents relating to clearing of imported goods at Sona Masjid, pursuant to provision of customs Act notices as point of law was duly produced in the High Court Division by supplementary affidavit but although these are issues of law pursuant to provision of customs Act were not taken into consideration and the Rule was discharged and continuation of the proceedings of the criminal case in the face of non-disclosure of commission of any offence and non-consideration of law involved in the mater is an abuse of the process of Court.
